title: Power Pages: client APIs for scripting forms, lists, users and data
notes: claim 48: fix was 1401 characters, cut to 1200
summary: The control paths, deployment commands and roadmap details are supported. The licensing discussion incorrectly leaves the applicability of Power Pages capacity licensing unresolved even though Microsoft identifies these client calls as Power Pages Web API operations and publishes the licensing rule for those operations.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Pages enforces table permissions on the server and the client API cannot override them.
claims.quote: Power Pages applies form metadata and table permissions on the server, and the client API can't override those settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Associated web roles determine the user's table permissions for Web API reads and writes.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated web role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Granting the Anonymous users web role table access exposes the table's data to visitors, subject to the stated tenant override.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.

claims.claim: The tenant Anonymous access to Dataverse control can override maker table permissions and prevent anonymous reads.
claims.quote: Selecting All sites blocks anonymous access in all the websites in the tenant, overriding any maker configurations that provide access to anonymous users.

claims.claim: Blocking anonymous viewing with that control does not prevent unauthenticated users from writing Dataverse data.
claims.quote: While unauthenticated users will be prevented from viewing Dataverse data when this setting is enabled, these users can still write data to Dataverse.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: setVisible(false) hides a control in the browser rather than securing its data.
claims.quote: The setVisible(false) method hides a control in the browser only. Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: row.setVisible(false) changes the displayed list rather than the data the server returns.
claims.quote: Hiding a row changes only what people see in the list; it doesn't change the data or the number of records that the server returns.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn instructs developers to protect data with table permissions and column security rather than presentation settings.
claims.quote: Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax includes the visitor's session cookie with every request.
claims.quote: Credentials: The session cookie is included with every request.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The specified client API pages name no licence, price or meter of their own.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "client API" "licensing" "webAPI"; read client-api overview, initialization, dataverse, user-authentication, ajax, agents and examples in full; those pages contain no licence, price or meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Pages licensing is capacity based, using authenticated and anonymous users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages licence.
claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license.

claims.claim: Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards anonymous user capacity.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards the anonymous user capacity.

claims.claim: Authenticated users making Web API calls need the applicable authenticated user capacity licences.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Learn does not establish whether the published Web API capacity licensing rule applies to $pages.webAPI.
claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license. For example, Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards the anonymous user capacity.
claims.fix: The cited wildcard troubleshooting page explicitly identifies $pages.webAPI.retrieveRecord and retrieveMultipleRecords as Power Pages Web API call patterns, so apply the published Web API licensing rule. Set licensing.model to 'mixed' and replace the licensing notes with: 'Power Pages uses authenticated and anonymous user capacity per website per month, with subscription and pay-as-you-go options. Web API operations require the applicable Power Pages capacity. Cloud flow integration requires a Power Automate licence. The client API reference publishes no separate client-API charge.' Replace 'Learn does not say whether that applies unchanged to $pages.webAPI' with 'These capacity requirements apply to $pages.webAPI operations; the troubleshooting guidance identifies these methods as Power Pages Web API calls.' In the cost rationale, replace 'the Power Pages capacity licensing position for client API calls is not stated' with 'Web API calls remain subject to Power Pages capacity licensing'. Remove the Open questions bullet questioning whether $pages.webAPI capacity accounting is published; do not imply a per-call charge. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/power-platfo…
